articles.body: Angular 20 end of support is on 28 November 2026. After that date the Angular team ships no more fixes for it, security fixes included. Angular 19 and every older version are already out of support. If your application runs on one of them, this is a good month to plan the move to Angular 22, the current major version. Angular support dates Each major Angular version gets six months of active support and then twelve months of long-term support (LTS), during which only critical and security fixes ship. The dates below come from the official Angular release schedule , checked on 23 November 2026.

articles.title: RaspAP's App Fingerprint Shows Why Default Router Checks Matter
articles.excerpt: RaspAP's App Fingerprint Shows Why Default Router Checks Matter RaspAP turns a Debian-based device into a wireless access point and management panel. Its official authentication documentation is unusu…
articles.body: RaspAP's App Fingerprint Shows Why Default Router Checks Matter RaspAP turns a Debian-based device into a wireless access point and management panel. Its official authentication documentation is unusually direct: the default administrator password is secret , the login should not be considered secure over plain HTTP and the default credentials are well known to third parties. That makes the management page a high-value asset even when the wireless network itself is separate. Authentication model RaspAP uses a password stored on the local filesystem and a session with an inactivity timeout. The documentation describes an experimental limited-privilege user who can manage a client connection but cannot change the rest of the configuration.
articles.author: kozhevniko

articles.title: .NET 8 end of support: should you upgrade to .NET 10 or .NET 11?
articles.excerpt: .NET 8 end of support arrived on 10 November 2026. On the same day Microsoft also stopped patching .NET 9 and shipped .NET 11. If your ASP.NET Core application still runs on .NET 8 or 9, it keeps work…
articles.body: .NET 8 end of support arrived on 10 November 2026. On the same day Microsoft also stopped patching .NET 9 and shipped .NET 11. If your ASP.NET Core application still runs on .NET 8 or 9, it keeps working, but it no longer gets fixes, including security fixes. This post covers what that means in practice, how .NET 10 and .NET 11 compare, and the upgrade plan I use on client projects. What end of support means for a running application Nothing breaks on the day support ends. The risk builds up afterwards.

Every week: the package names LLMs recommended that do not exist, and the ones somebody registered after a model said them. Every six hours VDB asks several LLMs for packages to use on ordinary tasks and checks each name against the registry. This is the week of Nov 16–22, 2026: 204 names seen for the first time, 10 produced again by at least one model, and 0 that somebody registered after a model had already recommended them. 2,293 names are live in the list in all. Most hallucinated this week Names a model produced this week, ranked by how many models agree on them. A name two models give is the one an attacker should expect to pay off.

articles.body: Hiring a remote senior .NET developer is different from filling a seat in the office. You will see less of how they work day to day, so the things that make someone senior have to show up in how they write, review and communicate. I have worked remotely for two and a half years for Smart Behan's branch in Oman, and I have been on both sides of code reviews and onboarding. These are the things I would check. 1. Do they own features end to end? A senior developer takes a feature from a vague requirement to a release without someone checking every step. Ask candidates to describe a feature they delivered: how they clarified the requirement, what they decided about the data and the API, how they tested it and what happened after release.

articles.title: Claude Code Context Deep Dive (2): Three Rules for the Message Array
articles.excerpt: Editor's note (November 2026): This article is an AI-assisted translation and adaptation of an older research note about Claude Code's message handling. Two statements in that note were too absolute:…
articles.body: Editor's note (November 2026): This article is an AI-assisted translation and adaptation of an older research note about Claude Code's message handling. Two statements in that note were too absolute: an application may transform or compact earlier messages rather than append forever, and the Anthropic Messages API does allow consecutive messages of the same role , combining them into one turn. The three “invariants” below are therefore presented as practical design rules, with the public API contract separated from version-specific Claude Code implementation observations. Part 1 described the agent loop: Claude Code assembles a request, receives a response, runs any requested client-side tools, and supplies results to a later model call. Now the message list itself is the subject.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified.
